```{r setup, include=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This workflow separates three questions:

1. where the adaptive optimum may have shifted;
2. whether evolutionary innovations are correlated among traits; and
3. how much uncertainty model and shift selection introduce.

See [getting started](getting-started.html) for input validation, observation
error, and the interpretation of search and bootstrap diagnostics.

## Prepare and fit correlated traits

`adjust_data()` normalizes branch lengths by default. Set `normalize = FALSE`
to keep the input time scale; otherwise the stored factor allows conversion of
rate estimates back to that scale. Repair remains a separate, opt-in operation.

```{r prepare-data, purl=FALSE}
library(kfl1ou)
data(lizard.tree, lizard.traits)

keep <- lizard.tree$tip.label[seq_len(12)]
tree <- ape::drop.tip(lizard.tree, setdiff(lizard.tree$tip.label, keep))
dat <- adjust_data(tree, lizard.traits[keep, 1:2], quietly = TRUE)
```

The default `trait.covariance = "diagonal"` fits separate trait likelihoods,
with a distinct alpha for each trait. `trait.covariance = "full"` estimates a
positive-definite evolutionary innovation covariance, `Omega`. With its
default `alpha.structure = "shared"`, the covariance is separable:
`Omega %x% C(alpha)`. `alpha.structure = "diagonal"` instead allows a distinct
adaptation rate for each trait while retaining correlated innovations. A
fully non-diagonal drift matrix is outside the implemented model.

The initial example fixes the configuration to zero shifts. A fixed fit does
not discover shifts; `search.max.nShifts` specifies the limit only if a later
method repeats shift selection. One optimizer start keeps this introductory
example quick; the calibration examples below use the default multiple starts.

```{r fixed-fit, purl=FALSE}
fit <- fit_OU(
  dat$tree, dat$Y, shift.configuration = integer(),
  criterion = "BIC", trait.covariance = "full",
  alpha.structure = "diagonal", likelihood.engine = "auto",
  optimizer.starts = 1, search.max.nShifts = 2
)

evolutionary_vcov(fit)
fit$tip.trait.correlation
original_time_parameters(fit)
```

`trait.covariance` and `trait.correlation` describe instantaneous innovations.
`tip.trait.covariance` and `tip.trait.correlation` describe the induced marginal
residual association at an ultrametric tip. When alpha differs among traits,
these are not generally equal. `joint.logLik` is the joint likelihood, not a
sum of independent trait likelihoods. Use `evolutionary_vcov()` for innovation
covariance; `vcov()` follows R's coefficient sampling-covariance convention.

## Likelihood engines, regularization and information criteria

Both `"dense"` and `"pruning"` support trait-specific missing entries, known
observation variances, estimated measurement error, and fixed or stationary
root models. `"auto"` retains the matrix-normal profile for complete,
unregularized shared-alpha data and chooses pruning for larger non-separable
problems. Explicit engine requests are honored. Pruning initialization and
`simulate(..., engine = "tree")` do not construct the full trait-by-tip
covariance matrix.

Full covariance needs enough residual contrasts. With n tips and p traits,
unregularized searches cap the number of shifts at n - p - 1; explicit invalid
fixed configurations still fail. Inspect `search.diagnostics$estimability`.
For many traits or few contrasts, `covariance.regularization = "shrinkage"`
can stabilize covariance estimates. `regularization.lambda` may be supplied or
estimated from phylogenetically whitened residuals. Dense and pruning engines
use the same correlation-penalty interpretation, including with missing data.

Full covariance supports ordinary BIC and a localization-aware multivariate
pBIC extension. In complete, unconstrained p-trait models, adding one shift
adds p mean parameters plus one location parameter to BIC, not always two.
Missingness and convergence constraints require the parameter-count and sample
size rules described by `configuration_ic()`. Multivariate pBIC is a sensitivity
criterion with an explicit branch-location penalty. Any information criterion
at a regularized estimate is also a sensitivity score rather than a calibrated
marginal-likelihood approximation; report comparisons with unregularized BIC.

```{r diagnostics, purl=FALSE}
diagnostics <- diagnose_l1ou(fit)
diagnostics[c("convergence", "boundary", "trait.covariance.condition")]
```

Boundary estimates, ill-conditioned covariance, or unavailable diagnostics need
investigation. `profile_alpha_l1ou()`, `profile_measurement_error_l1ou()`, and
`sensitivity_l1ou()` help assess weak identification. For simulation-calibrated
checks, pass an adequate `nsim` to `diagnose_l1ou()` or
`check_rate_heterogeneity()`; `nsim = 0` skips calibration.

## Covariance comparison with shift selection

The remaining blocks are intentionally not run during ordinary vignette
builds, because hundreds of complete searches are expensive. Choose the
simulation count and search limits for the scientific question. Development
smoke checks execute these same blocks with only a few simulations; those
counts are insufficient for inference.

```{r simulation-count, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
n_replicates <- 200L
```

`compare_trait_covariance()` never selects shifts on the observed data. Its
`shift.configuration` defaults to no shifts, and `selection` defaults to
`"conditional"`. To include selection in this comparison, first run the same
**diagonal-covariance BIC search** used inside its bootstrap. Pass the selected
configuration, search limit, root model and search strategy explicitly.
If using observation error, pass the same error settings to both calls as well.

```{r covariance-comparison, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
max_shifts <- 2L
search_strategy <- "auto"
root_model <- "OUfixedRoot"
null_search <- estimate_shift_configuration(
  dat$tree, dat$Y, max.nShifts = max_shifts, criterion = "BIC",
  trait.covariance = "diagonal", root.model = root_model,
  search.strategy = search_strategy
)
comparison <- compare_trait_covariance(
  dat$tree, dat$Y,
  shift.configuration = null_search$shift.configuration,
  selection = "full", search.max.nShifts = max_shifts,
  search.strategy = search_strategy, root.model = root_model,
  alpha.structure = "diagonal",
  nboot = n_replicates, seed = 1, nCores = 2
)
comparison[c("selection", "search.max.nShifts", "successful", "failed",
             "failure.messages", "p.value", "p.value.mcse")]
```

Both observed-data fits use `null_search$shift.configuration`. Each null
simulation reselects shifts with diagonal covariance and BIC, then refits both
covariance models to that replicate's selected configuration. Thus observed
and simulated data use the same selection rule. For a prespecified fixed
configuration, use `selection = "conditional"` instead. A separate shift search
using full covariance is not automatically inherited by this comparison.
The default trait-specific-alpha full model nests the diagonal model; a
shared-alpha full alternative is non-nested and needs bootstrap calibration.
Regularized comparisons are reported as sensitivity analyses.

## Uncertainty after a full-covariance shift search

For inference under the full-covariance model itself, discover its shifts
separately. The comparison above addresses a different selection procedure.
This small example allows at most one shift to keep its running time manageable;
choose a suitable limit for the scientific question and inspect search coverage.

```{r correlated-search, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
fit_correlated <- estimate_shift_configuration(
  dat$tree, dat$Y, max.nShifts = 1, criterion = "BIC",
  trait.covariance = "full", alpha.structure = "diagonal",
  likelihood.engine = "auto", search.strategy = "auto"
)
fit_correlated$search.diagnostics
```

```{r bootstrap, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
support <- l1ou_bootstrap_support(
  fit_correlated, nItrs = n_replicates, type = "parametric", seed = 2,
  multicore = TRUE, nCores = 2
)
support[c("attempted", "successful", "failed", "failure.messages")]
summarize_shift_uncertainty(support, dat$tree)
```

```{r full-intervals, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
intervals <- confint(
  fit_correlated, method = "parametric", selection = "full",
  interval = "basic", nsim = n_replicates, seed = 3
)
intervals
attr(intervals, "failed")
attr(intervals, "failure.messages")
```

These resamples repeat the stored full-covariance search and its one-shift
limit. Inspect failed refits, boundary estimates, and the effective number of
samples per interval. Exact-edge coefficients and canonical tip partitions
answer different questions: equivalent placements should not be interpreted
as biological disagreement. Report tree/root-model sensitivity and which
candidate configurations were evaluated. Exact historical shift timing is
not identifiable from extant-tip data alone.
